data.narrative: The student successfully implemented the Cache-Aside caching strategy with Redis, balancing read performance with memory efficiency. They demonstrated robust production thinking by implementing graceful degradation (DB fallbacks when Redis is offline) and resolved a stale-cache bug by adding explicit cache invalidation on updates.

dimension_scores.observation: Correctly chose Cache-Aside over Write-Through to prevent memory bloat from dead links in a read-heavy workload.
dimension_scores.evidence: Chose Option A because a URL shortener has a massive read-heavy workload where many created links may never be clicked.

dimension_scores.observation: Reproduced the stale cache bug by omitting invalidation on PATCH, observed the stale redirect, and successfully closed it with a targeted fix and regression test.
dimension_scores.evidence: Injected the missing invalidation, ran a test showing the old URL was served, restored the delete call, and proved correct redirection to the new URL.

dimension_scores.observation: Understood the risks of caching protected resources and the importance of tenant scoping in cache keys.
dimension_scores.evidence: Answered verification questions regarding the risks of caching auth-protected data without tenant scoping.

dimension_scores.observation: Implemented strict fallback logic ensuring Redis failures degrade performance gracefully rather than causing hard outages.
dimension_scores.evidence: Wrapped cache operations in try/except blocks falling back to database reads on timeouts.

dimension_scores.observation: Clearly articulated why cache invalidation is notoriously difficult in distributed systems.
dimension_scores.evidence: Answered verification questions explaining how missed mutation paths lead to data drift.

strengths: Designing fault-tolerant graceful degradation for cache outages
Scripting reproducible regression tests for stale data bugs
data.recommendation: When scaling to multiple Redis nodes, consider implementing cache key namespaces and connection pooling optimizations to handle high-concurrency traffic spikes.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented Cache-Aside pattern with Redis for short link redirects, complete with explicit cache invalidation on updates and database fallback on Redis failure.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Configured aioredis with timeout limits, added get_redirect_target, set_redirect_target, and invalidate_redirect_target helper functions, and wrapped calls in try/except blocks for fail-open resilience.
public_evidence.proof: Regression test output showing initial cache miss/set, successful cache hit, cache invalidation on PATCH /api/links/{code}, and seamless DB fallback when REDIS_URL is unreachable.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves the candidate knows how to optimize read-heavy paths with caching while building the necessary fault-tolerance and invalidation guardrails to prevent data staleness and hard outages.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Implemented explicit cache deletion on link updates.

teaching_approaches.detail: Injected a bug omitting cache invalidation on PATCH to demonstrate staleness.

learning_style_signals: Thrives when building complete end-to-end failure drills that test both performance optimizations and failure modes.
